title.narrative: Fortaleciendo la seguridad de la fauna silvestre amenazada y su hbitat a travs del.empoderamiento local en el Paisaje de los Bosques Lluviosos Ancestrales, Selva Maya, Guatemala

description.narrative: Process will secure long-term conservation of the Ancestral Rainforests Landscape of the Guatemalan Maya Forest and its rich wildlife by empowering local Maya-Qeqchis in community wildlife and forest management. The work is intended to strengthen indigenous stewardship of wildlife and their habitat across a landscape at risk from megaprojects, expansion of monoculture, and illegal wildlife trade. Specific activities include: 1) in-depth consultations and workshops with over 100 local and regional authorities from 33 communities in Ixcn on the rules and regulations related to hunting, consumption and commerce of endangered wildlife to empower them to establish community-based conservation agreements that prohibit illegal wildlife harvest and trade as well as sale of land for African Palm monoculture, large-scale cattle ranches, and megaprojects; 2) educate and empower 10 local Maya Qeqchi youth as conservation champions through hands-on training in sustainable natural resource management practices and culturally relevant leadership skills; 3) train 8 park guards to carry out biological monitoring of key mammal indicator species within Laguna Lachua National Park; and 4) evaluate impact by monitoring ecological and social indicators in the study region.
